newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway oil union accepts wage deal. [corrected 09:35 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Norway oil union accepts wage deal. [corrected 09:35 GMT]

text.p: The union for production and automation technicians working on Norway's offshore oil and gas platforms said on Monday it would accept a wage offer from employers, bringing to an end this year's wage negotiations in the offshore sector.
Jan Olav Brekke, union leader for the Norwegian Association of Supervisors (NALF), said regional representatives voted at the weekend for a settlement with the Oil Industry Confederation (OLF).

Earlier in June, Norway's two other major offshore unions -- the Norwegian Oil and Petrochemical Union (NOPEF) and the Federation of Norwegian Oil Workers (OFS) -- accepted OLF's offer of a rise of 8,900 crowns ($1,220) per year and a two crown increase in shift allowance to 34 crowns per hour.

NALF initially refused the deal because of disagreement over compensation for workers, who have argued that their responsibilities and duties increased following a reorganisation of jobs on the platforms.
"Two out of 24 of the representatives voted not to accept the deal. (corrects to insert omitted negation) I will probably sign it later today," Brekke told Reuters.
NALF has around 800 members working on most of the installations on the Norwegian continental shelf.
Norway, with current oil output ranging between 3.0 and 3.2 million barrels per day (bpd), is western Europe's largest oil producer and the world's second biggest oil exporter after Saudi Arabia.
-- Tanya Pang, Oslo newsroom, +47 22 42 50 41 ($ = 7.260 Norwegian Crowns)
